correctness.rationale: Laplacian block-squaring and eigenspace decomposition yield four exactly necessary/sufficient Markov positivity inequalities and the three SLEM values. The equioscillation sign-variation proof gives unique unconstrained optimum, including the equal-part degeneracy. A high-degree-diagonal active-constraint perturbation argument certifies strict global optimality and uniqueness beyond q=p^2/(p-2). Algebra at the boundary and asymptotic comparison are exact. Standalone independent linear programming, rational arithmetic and Laplacian matrix checker completed 14,188 assertions, which corroborate but do not replace proof.

evidence: Boyd–Diaconis–Parrilo–Xiao, arxiv:0709.0955v1, Section 3.1.2 gives an exact one-hop transition probability alpha=min(1/q,2/(q+2p)) on K_{p,q}.

Boyd–Diaconis–Xiao, SIAM Review 46 (2004), imposes support on original graph edges and studies symmetric stochastic one-hop kernels; its general SDP can represent a two-hop support relaxation but not the exact two-coefficient polynomial restriction without added constraints.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The two-hop squared graph of K_{p,q} is complete, so the unrestricted stochastic-kernel problem is solved by uniform averaging with SLEM zero. This more permissive result does not imply the optimum among quadratic polynomials of the original Laplacian. The one-hop graph result also does not contain the two-hop within-part transitions.

originality.rationale: The known unconstrained quadratic spectral minimax and standard one-hop fastest-mixing results are treated as prior art. Their feasibility sets do not contain the entrywise-nonnegative completed quadratic-filter constraint analyzed here. The new all-biclique holding-probability threshold, uniqueness of the saturated branch and quantified separation from two individually stochastic Euler factors are not asserted by the inspected primary texts. Searches found no equivalent statement; incomplete indexing remains a residual originality risk.
residual_risks: The literature index and local publication searches are not exhaustive, and a differently worded constrained-polynomial special case could exist.
The prior unconstrained branch is established prior art and is explicitly not presented as an independent novelty.
The requirement that the combined polynomial kernel be nonnegative allows signed intermediate evaluations; the result should not be interpreted as a stagewise-positive algorithm.

value.rationale: The constrained polynomial kernel is a natural Markov-valid two-hop filter. The theorem explains a sharp graph-imbalance transition from unconstrained Chebyshev-style oscillation to saturated zero-holding probabilities, for all K_{p,q} with p,q>=2, with a closed-form globally unique optimizer. Its nonfactorizable performance is quantitatively meaningful: at fixed p>=3 and growing q the filter SLEM tends below 1/2 while every pair of individually stochastic one-hop steps has SLEM tending to one. It is not just re-solving an already tabulated small instance.
